en.html:
Today the coast was cool.
Compared with yesterday, another world only. Still not cold enough for the season written on the calendar, but short sleeves had become a decision one could regret.

At this extraordinary change in temperature, the locals merely sighed. Gloomily. I asked; this too happened often, they said.
...Since Enoshima had gone wrong.

en.html:
Ichijou and I stood side by side, looking across at the island.
Entry was for night. In the daylight, at least some information I would have liked to collect. But today the bathers were absent, and the shops serving them had shut their doors also. For asking questions, a fine supply of nobody.

Time going to waste was regrettable. Regret would not improve the supply.

Very irritating, this business of waiting correctly. Wait calmly, and nothing happens. Wait furiously, and exactly the same nothing happens, but now you have worked hard at it. Kya mehnat hai. Such labour. By evening a man can be thoroughly exhausted without having advanced beyond the place where he first became annoyed.

No impatience. Wait, that was all we could do.

en.html:
Her own feelings she was not reporting. That much I understood immediately.
She meant the condition around us.

Before noon, a coast like this ought to be busy with people fishing. Instead, boats that did not go to sea. A few fishermen who only looked at the sea. And between the two, this emptiness.

Probably this was the true face of Katase Beach now. Yesterday's bustle had been provided by people with no connection to the place. Visitors came, noise came; visitors went, and this remained.

Beautiful Enoshima had been taken from them. Its gateway also was withering.
Kyun? For what?

en.html: An accusation with no possible denial. —Yes. Rokuhara's tyranny was wrong. Search any government for faults, and you could go on forever. Even rulers like Rokuhara were better than no rulers. Given the world's condition, military government could hardly be avoided.◆ ...For Rokuhara's defence, arguments were available in full stock. But against this accusation, straight and unhesitating as a needle, what wall could all that cleverness build? Dress it however you liked, the fact remained: they were wrong. They were doing wrong. The wrong of inhumanity. Those clever defences were not really protecting the shogunate. They protected the person speaking. The helplessness, the humiliation of being unable to condemn the shogunate to its face—usse bachna tha. That was what he wished to escape. So much reasoning, to hide himself behind it. This girl would not give it one glance. Neither the enemy's evil nor her own powerlessness would she look away from. The truth she meant to carry through, all the way. A strength so great it was almost strange.
en.text:
An accusation with no possible denial.

—Yes. Rokuhara's tyranny was wrong.

Search any government for faults, and you could go on forever.
Even rulers like Rokuhara were better than no rulers.
Given the world's condition, military government could hardly be avoided.◆
...For Rokuhara's defence, arguments were available in full stock.

But against this accusation, straight and unhesitating as a needle, what wall could all that cleverness build? Dress it however you liked, the fact remained: they were wrong. They were doing wrong.
The wrong of inhumanity.

Those clever defences were not really protecting the shogunate. They protected the person speaking. The helplessness, the humiliation of being unable to condemn the shogunate to its face—usse bachna tha. That was what he wished to escape. So much reasoning, to hide himself behind it.
This girl would not give it one glance.

Neither the enemy's evil nor her own powerlessness would she look away from. The truth she meant to carry through, all the way.
A strength so great it was almost strange.

否定の仕様もない弾劾。
　
　――そう。六波羅の圧政は、間違っている。

　どのような政府でも瑕瑾を探せばきりがない、
　六波羅のような統治者でもいないよりはまし、
　現今の世界情勢を思えば軍事政権もやむなし、◆
　……六波羅とて、弁護の余地はいくらでもある。

　が、そんな賢しらな理屈が、この針の如く迷いない
弾劾に対して、何の壁になるだろう。
　どう言い繕おうが、彼らが間違っているのは事実な
のだ――誤りを犯しているのは事実なのだ。

　非道という誤りを。

　小賢しい弁護はその実、幕府を守るためのものでは
なく、面と向かって幕府の誤りを非難できない無力感、
屈辱感から己を守るためのものである。
　そんなものに、この少女は一顧だにくれない。

　敵の邪悪からも己の無力からも目を逸らさず、真実
を貫徹せんとする。
　それは異奇なまでの、勁つよさといえた。

en.html:
Along the shore we walked.
Only Kanae accompanied me. The others were doing their work separately.

A stroll this was not meant to be. Information for tonight, that was the idea. But people to question were in short supply. Probably the cool air had driven off the unseasonable bathers.

At a suitable point, we should stop. The intention to investigate could not investigate itself.

en.html:
Kageaki"Shall we turn back?"
Kanae"A little longer looking at the sea, perhaps?"
Kageaki"On the way back also, the sea can be seen."
Kanae"Haaye, what a natural talent. A lady's heart beneath your feet, and you don't even notice the bump... So wonderfully obtuse. I am quite, quite dizzy."
Kageaki"Are you unwell, Captain?"
Kanae"Your charm is confusing me, Mr. Kageaki. Is this... love?"
Kageaki"Misunderstanding. Please keep your senses in their proper place."
Kanae"Just standing beside you, dhak-dhak, my heart is racing! Meri baat hi nahi sunta. It won't listen to me... Ah, what has happened to me?"
Kageaki"Some variety of heart trouble appears possible. A doctor's opinion you should obtain."
Kanae"Not THAT...! This garden of thorns in my breast—surely one sincere word from Mr. Kageaki would...!"
Kageaki(A sincere word...)
Kanae"..."
Kageaki"You have lost your senses."
Kanae"Achha. Sincerity received. That will do. Let us rest a little."
Kageaki"Yes."

Kageaki"That you enjoyed it is fortunate. A joke I had not intended."
Kanae"Yes... truly. That was most entertaining."
Kanae"In return, something entertaining from me also. A story."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Once upon a time, deep in the mountains, there lived a demon."
Kanae"Such strength this demon had. Boar, bear, neither could match it. In time, lord of the mountain they called it, and feared it."
Kanae"Then toward the villages it looked. Humans also should see its strength, no? That desire had come."
Kanae"Down the mountain it came, and ravaged the village at its foot. People killed. Homes destroyed. What it had done, the survivors were left to bear."
Kanae"With the greatest delight, they say, it laid waste to that village."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"But the village's lord was a brave samurai. To protect his people, boldly he faced the demon."
Kanae"The demon was strong. The lord lost, was wounded, lost again. Still he would not give up. At last, with a mountain hermit's help, he brought the demon down."
Kanae"Everyone rejoiced. Then, before long, a troublesome matter came to their attention."
Kanae"Some survivors, they decided, had been tainted by the demon. Khatra abhi baaki hai. The danger remained, they said. Those people carried it with them. That was the verdict."
Kanae"So the lord gathered those survivors and burned them to death. Most reluctantly, of course. With tears. The hermit had advised it: the souls the demon had defiled must be purified."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Thus peace returned to the village. A living god, they called the lord, and worshipped him. After his death they enshrined him, and a real god he became, they say."
Kanae"And they all lived happily ever after."
